<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for this personal finance tool called "Actual." Here's how to approach it:

1. Main System Components
The diagram should highlight these key components:

a) Core Application Layer:
- Entry point (app.js)
- Account Management System (src/accounts/*)
- Authentication Systems (password.js and openid.js)
- Database Layer (src/db.js, src/account-db.js)
- Migration System (migrations/*)

b) Integration Services:
- GoCardless Banking Integration (src/app-gocardless/*)
- SimpleFin Integration (src/app-simplefin/*)
- Sync Service (src/app-sync/*)

c) Security Layer:
- Secrets Management (src/app-secrets.js)
- User Service (src/services/user-service.js)

2. Architectural Patterns to Highlight

The diagram should emphasize:
- Local-First Architecture: Show the local storage and sync mechanisms
- Multi-User Support: Illustrate user isolation and management
- Banking Integration Framework: Display the pluggable bank adapter system
- Migration System: Show the database evolution path

3. Component Relationships

Draw these key interactions:
```
[Client Applications] ←→ [Sync Service]
                           ↕
                    [Core Server Layer]
                           ↕
         [Banking APIs] ←→ [Integration Layer]
                           ↕
                    [Database Layer]
```

4. Specific Implementation Details

Use different shapes/colors to represent:
- Blue rectangles: Core services
- Green diamonds: External integrations
- Yellow cylinders: Data stores
- Red hexagons: Security components
- Purple clouds: Third-party services

5. Key Flows to Illustrate

a) Authentication Flow:
```
User → OpenID/Password Auth → Token Generation → Protected Resources
```

b) Banking Integration Flow:
```
Bank API → GoCardless Adapter → Bank Factory → Core Services
```

c) Sync Flow:
```
Client → Sync Service → File Service → Database
```

6. Additional Considerations

Include these elements:
- Docker container boundaries (shown as dotted lines)
- Database migration paths
- Security boundaries
- API endpoints
- Configuration management

7. Legend Section

Create a legend explaining:
- All shapes and colors used
- Connection types (REST, internal calls, etc.)
- Security boundaries
- Container boundaries

8. Technical Stack Indicators

Mark technologies used:
- Node.js runtime
- SQL database
- REST APIs
- OpenID Connect
- Docker containerization

The diagram should maintain a high-level view while showing the modular nature of the system, especially the banking integration framework which appears to be a significant part of the architecture.

Remember to:
- Use clear, consistent naming
- Show data flow directions
- Indicate async operations
- Mark security boundaries
- Include version/migration paths
- Show scaling points

This will create a comprehensive yet understandable diagram that accurately represents the system's architecture while highlighting its local-first nature and synchronization capabilities.
